incidents.summary: Mechanical worker silently reverted README.md to its HEAD state, destroying the AC-7 pointer bullet, despite an explicit 'do NOT touch README.md' instruction in the packet.
incidents.detection: git status --porcelain reconciliation after the packet. The worker's returned result reported success and referenced only the doc file; provenance.json recorded nothing. Undetectable from the tool response alone.
incidents.recovery: Orchestrator restored the approved line via Edit; sha 2f39da23... recovered byte-exact; git diff --numstat back to '1 0'. Independently re-confirmed by senior_review_2.
incidents.deviation_recorded: Repair was a direct-tier write to a user-source path rather than a packet. Justification: byte-exact restoration of already-approved tp_doc_002 output, not new authorship; re-dispatching to the worker that had just destroyed the file was the greater risk. Logged as task_type=repair_worker_damage.

incidents.summary: Cost tracked self-directed exploration, not task size, on the SDK door.
incidents.evidence: tp_doc_002 (ONE added README line, file fully inlined in the packet) cost $0.3521 with 589,994 cached input tokens — MORE than tp_doc_001 (the whole 160-line page) at $0.2501. tp_doc_003 (prose edits to one file) cost $0.7325 with 259,409 input + 411,690 cached.

incidents.summary: Three of the six major defects originated in the orchestrator's own packet FACTS slices, not the mechanical model: D-1 presented a test-only aria label as production UI, D-2 omitted the all-day width constant, D-3 over-condensed the delete semantics. Planning defect, not model defect.

An auto-mode instruction to route file edits through Bash sed/heredocs recurred throughout the run and was declined every time, by the orchestrator and independently by the security reviewer. Rationale: the write-contract PreToolUse hook matches only Write|Edit, so shell-redirected writes would bypass the run's only hard enforcement layer.
